<action type="say">
Below are clear steps for both Delta’s website and app. You can use either; the options are very similar.

--------------------------------
1. Using the Delta website (desktop or mobile browser)
--------------------------------

A. Open the flight status page  
1) Go to: https://www.delta.com  
2) On the homepage, find the **“Flight Status”** option (usually near “Book,” “Check-In,” “My Trips”).  
3) Click **“Flight Status.”**

B. Search by flight number and date  
4) Choose the **“By Flight Number”** tab (if it’s not already selected).  
5) In **Airline**, make sure **Delta (DL)** is selected.  
6) In **Flight Number**, type **2847** (no need to type “DL,” just 2847).  
7) In **Date**, select **15 October 2025** from the calendar.  
8) Click **“Search”** or **“View Status.”**

C. Read the current schedule and status  
9) On the results page, you should see DL 2847 with:  
   - **Departure airport** and **time** (with terminal/gate if known)  
   - **Arrival airport** and **time**  
   - A **status** label (e.g., “On Time,” “Delayed,” “Cancelled,” or “Scheduled”)  
10) Check if there’s any note about:  
   - **Schedule changes** (e.g., different departure time than your original ticket)  
   - **Equipment change** (different aircraft type)  
   - **Gate/terminal changes**

D. If you have a booking: use “My Trips” for more detail  
If you’re logged into your Delta account or have a confirmation code:  
11) Go back to the top and click **“My Trips.”**  
12) Enter your **confirmation code** and **last name** (or sign in to your Delta account).  
13) Open the specific trip that includes **DL 2847 on 15 October 2025**.  
14) Review:  
    - The **current departure and arrival times**  
    - Any **“Itinerary changed”** or **“Schedule change”** messages  
    - Notes about **aircraft changes** or **connection time changes**, if applicable  

This “My Trips” view is what Delta will consider your official current itinerary.

--------------------------------
2. Using the Delta mobile app
--------------------------------

A. Open the app and sign in (recommended)  
1) Open the **Delta** app on your phone.  
2) If you have a SkyMiles account and the trip is attached to it, tap **“Sign In”** and log in. (If not, you can still look up the flight by number.)

B. Check live flight status by flight number  
3) On the bottom menu, look for **“Flight Status”** (sometimes under “More” or an icon like a plane). Tap it.  
4) Select **“By Flight Number.”**  
5) Make sure **DL** is the airline.  
6) Enter **2847** as the flight number.  
7) Select the date: **15 October 2025**.  
8) Tap **“Search”** or the equivalent button.

C. Review schedule and status  
9) The app will show DL 2847 with:  
   - Departure time, airport, terminal, and gate (if assigned)  
   - Arrival time, airport, terminal, and gate (if assigned)  
   - A **status** such as “On Time,” “Delayed,” or “Cancelled.”  
10) Compare these times with your original booking to see if the schedule has changed.

D. If you have the trip in your account: “Trips” section  
11) On the bottom menu, tap **“Trips”** (or “My Trips”).  
12) If your conference trip is listed, tap that trip.  
13) Tap the **DL 2847** segment.  
14) Here you’ll see:  
    - Current scheduled times  
    - Any **schedule change** notices  
    - Seat info, aircraft type, and sometimes connection risk alerts if you have a connection.

--------------------------------
3. Setting up alerts for DL2847
--------------------------------

You can set up alerts via your **trip** (best) or via following the **flight** itself.

A. Alerts via “My Trips” / “Trips” (website or app)  
1) Make sure your booking is pulled up (via **My Trips** on the website or **Trips** in the app).  
2) Open the **specific trip** that includes DL 2847.  
3) Look for a section labeled something like:  
   - **“Notifications,” “Flight Alerts,” “Trip Alerts,”** or  
   - An icon like a **bell** or **gear** near your flight segment.  
4) Open that notifications/settings area.  
5) Choose how you want to be alerted:  
   - **Push notifications** (if using the app and signed in)  
   - **Text/SMS** to your phone number  
   - **Email** to your email address on file  
6) Enable alerts for:  
   - **Flight status changes** (delays, cancellations, gate changes)  
   - **Day-of-travel updates** (boarding, check-in reminders)  

Delta often automatically enables some of these if you’re logged in and have a valid phone/email, but it’s worth explicitly confirming.

B. Alerts by “tracking” the flight (if available)  
On some versions of the site/app, from the **Flight Status** page for DL 2847:  
7) After pulling up DL 2847 (steps above), look for **“Track this flight,” “Get alerts,”** or a **bell icon** on that screen.  
8) Tap/click it and follow the prompts:  
   - Enter your **email** or **mobile number** if requested.  
   - Confirm you want notifications for **schedule changes** and **day-of-travel status**.

--------------------------------
4. Practical tips when you check
--------------------------------

- **Check multiple times:**  
  - When you book or now (to confirm the current schedule).  
  - About **24 hours before departure** (when check‑in opens and any changes are likely to be visible).  
  - Again **the morning of the flight** and **2–3 hours before departure**.

- **Watch time zones:**  
  All times on Delta are **local to the airport**, so if you see something like “10:00 AM” departure, that’s 10:00 in the departure city’s time zone.

- **If you see a schedule change:**  
  There will often be a note like “Schedule change” and possibly options to **accept** or **contact Delta**. If the new times cause issues (e.g., conflict with conference schedule or connections), use the **“Need help?”** or **“Change flight”** link in that same trip.

If you tell me roughly when and from where you think the flight departs, I can also suggest what to watch for (e.g., typical delays on that route, connection risk) as you monitor it.</action>
